title: What If You Fell Into Jupiter?
description:
Jupiter has no solid ground. Fall in from far away and its gravity would speed you up to nearly 60 km every second before you reach the cloud tops (Jupiter's escape velocity is about 59.5 km/s). In 1995 NASA's Galileo probe did exactly this: it plunged into the clouds and sent back data for about 58 minutes before it went silent, crushed and overheated far below the cloud tops. Thousands of kilometres deeper, the pressure is so high that hydrogen is squeezed into a liquid that conducts electricity like a metal.

Sources: NASA Jupiter fact sheet (escape velocity 59.5 km/s); NASA, Galileo probe entry (7 December 1995, 58 minutes of data); NASA Juno mission on metallic hydrogen.
Narration is AI-generated (ElevenLabs) and the pictures and opening clip are AI-generated. This is a thought experiment.
